# Master Services Agreement
Contract ID: CTR-2026-0055
Supplier: Vantage Point Consulting Group LLC
Tax ID: 45-8812093
Contract Owner: P. Dubois, VP of Procurement
Total Contract Value: $875,000 USD
Contract Validity Period: 2026-01-15 to 2029-01-14
Vendor Risk Tier: Tier 1 — Critical (per POL-VRM-005)

## 1. Scope of Work
Vantage Point Consulting Group LLC ("Vendor") shall provide enterprise
digital transformation advisory services, including business process
reengineering, technology roadmap development, change management support,
and program governance for the Company's Finance and Operations
modernization initiative, as further detailed in Exhibits A through D.
Services shall be delivered across three phases: Discovery (Months 1-3),
Design (Months 4-9), and Implementation Support (Months 10-24).

## 2. Term and Renewal
This Agreement commences on the Effective Date and continues for 36 months
unless terminated earlier per Section 9. The Agreement may be renewed for
successive 12-month terms upon mutual written agreement, subject to the
renewal review requirements of SOP-CR-012, including reconfirmation of
Vendor's risk tier status and reapplication of then-current Procurement
Policy approval thresholds.

## 3. Payment Terms
### 3.1 Fee Structure
Total not-to-exceed contract value is $875,000, allocated as follows:
- Discovery Phase: $150,000, invoiced in two equal installments upon
  kickoff and phase completion
- Design Phase: $350,000, invoiced monthly at $58,333.33 based on
  percentage-of-completion against the agreed project plan
- Implementation Support Phase: $375,000, invoiced monthly at $26,785.71
  over 14 months

### 3.2 Payment Schedule
All invoices are due Net 30 from receipt. No advance payment is authorized
under this Agreement. Invoices must include time and expense detail
sufficient for Company's Finance team to reconcile against the phase
budget above.

### 3.3 Expense Reimbursement
Pre-approved travel and out-of-pocket expenses shall be reimbursed at cost,
capped at 8% of the applicable phase fee, and must be submitted with
receipts within 60 days of being incurred.

## 4. Deliverables
1. Current-state assessment report (end of Discovery)
2. Future-state process design documentation (end of Design)
3. Technology roadmap and implementation plan (end of Design)
4. Monthly implementation status reports (Implementation Support phase)
5. Change management training materials and delivery
6. Final program closeout report

## 5. Key Personnel
Vendor shall assign a named Engagement Lead and Program Manager for the
duration of the engagement. Substitution of either role requires Company's
prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, and Vendor must
provide a minimum 2-week transition/knowledge-transfer period for any
approved substitution.

## 6. Vendor Risk and Security Requirements
As a Tier 1 vendor under the Vendor Risk Management Policy (POL-VRM-005),
Vendor shall:
1. Maintain a current SOC 2 Type II report, provided to the Company
   annually and upon request
2. Participate in an annual security audit conducted by or on behalf of
   the Company
3. Maintain a documented business continuity and disaster recovery plan,
   reviewed with the Company annually
4. Notify the Company of any actual or suspected security incident
   affecting Company data within 24 hours of discovery — a shorter window
   than the standard 72-hour requirement in POL-SEC-002, reflecting this
   engagement's elevated risk tier
5. Disclose all subcontractors granted access to Company data prior to
   granting such access, per POL-VRM-005 Section 5

## 7. Data Privacy and Confidentiality
### 7.1 Data Handling
Vendor shall access Company data solely to perform the Services and shall
not use, disclose, or retain such data for any other purpose. Data shall be
classified per the Company's data classification scheme, and Vendor shall
apply security controls appropriate to the highest classification level of
data accessed.

### 7.2 Retention and Destruction
Upon completion of each phase, Vendor shall purge working data no longer
required for the current phase. Upon termination or expiration of this
Agreement, Vendor shall return or certify destruction of all Company data
within 30 days, consistent with POL-VRM-005 Section 7.

### 7.3 Breach Notification
Vendor shall notify the Company within 24 hours of discovering any breach
or suspected breach involving Company data, and shall cooperate fully with
the Company's incident response process, including providing all relevant
logs and forensic information upon request.

### 7.4 Regulatory Compliance
Vendor shall comply with all applicable data protection regulations
including GDPR and CCPA where the underlying data subjects fall within
those regulations' scope, and shall support the Company's response to any
data subject access requests within 5 business days of request.

### 7.5 Audit Rights
The Company, or its designated third-party auditor, may audit Vendor's data
handling and security practices no more than twice per 12-month period upon
15 days written notice, or immediately following a security incident.

## 8. Confidentiality
Both parties shall keep confidential all non-public information disclosed
under this Agreement, consistent with the Confidentiality Policy
(POL-CONF-004), for a period of 3 years following termination or
expiration of this Agreement.

## 9. Termination
### 9.1 Termination for Convenience
Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon 60 days
written notice, given the scale and multi-phase nature of the engagement.

### 9.2 Termination for Cause
Either party may terminate immediately upon written notice if the other
party materially breaches this Agreement and fails to cure within 15 days
of written notice of the breach.

### 9.3 Effect of Termination
Upon termination, Vendor shall be paid for Services satisfactorily
performed through the termination date, and shall comply with the data
return/destruction obligations in Section 7.2.

## 10. Liability and Indemnification
### 10.1 Limitation of Liability
Except for breaches of Section 7 (Data Privacy and Confidentiality) or
Section 8 (Confidentiality), or claims arising from gross negligence or
willful misconduct, each party's aggregate liability under this Agreement
shall not exceed the total fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding
the claim.

### 10.2 Indemnification
Vendor shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the Company from any
third-party claims arising from Vendor's breach of this Agreement,
negligence, or willful misconduct in the performance of Services.

## 11. Insurance
Vendor shall maintain insurance coverage consistent with Tier 1
requirements under POL-VRM-005 Section 6, and shall provide certificates
of insurance to the Company prior to commencement of Services and upon
each policy renewal.

## 12. Governing Law and Dispute Resolution
This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the state in which the
Company's headquarters is located. Any disputes arising under this
Agreement shall first be escalated to each party's designated executive
sponsor for good-faith resolution before either party pursues formal
dispute resolution.

## 13. Miscellaneous
This Agreement, together with its Exhibits, constitutes the entire
agreement between the parties regarding its subject matter and supersedes
all prior negotiations or agreements. Amendments must be in writing and
signed by authorized representatives of both parties. Neither party may
assign this Agreement without the other's prior written consent, except in
connection with a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets.

## Approval
Approved by: P. Dubois, VP of Procurement
Legal Review: Completed 2026-01-08, K. Whitfield, Senior Counsel
CFO Sign-off: Completed 2026-01-10, M. Alvarado, CFO
Date of Execution: 2026-01-14

# Software License and Support Agreement
Contract ID: CTR-2026-0071
Supplier: Larkspur Analytics Inc.
Tax ID: 88-4471029
Contract Owner: H. Talbi, Procurement
Total Contract Value: $142,800 USD
Contract Validity Period: 2026-03-15 to 2027-03-14
Vendor Risk Tier: Tier 2 — High (per POL-VRM-005)

## 1. License Grant
Larkspur Analytics Inc. grants the Company a non-exclusive, non-transferable
license to use the Larkspur Insights Platform for up to 250 named users
across the Company's Finance and Operations departments, for the duration
of this Agreement.

## 2. Fees
Annual license fee: $120,000, invoiced upfront upon execution. Annual
support and maintenance fee: $22,800 (19% of license fee), invoiced upfront
alongside the license fee. Total first-year contract value: $142,800.

## 3. Support Terms
Vendor shall provide Business Hours support (8am-6pm ET, Monday-Friday)
with a 4-hour response time for Severity 1 issues and 1-business-day
response for Severity 2 and below. Vendor shall provide quarterly platform
updates and shall notify the Company at least 30 days in advance of any
update requiring user retraining.

## 4. Data Privacy and Confidentiality
As the platform will process Company financial and operational data
classified as Confidential, Vendor shall: restrict data use solely to
providing the licensed services; retain Company data only for the duration
of the Agreement plus 30 days for transition purposes; notify the Company
of any breach within 72 hours of discovery; comply with applicable data
protection regulations; and permit the Company to audit data handling
practices with 15 days notice, consistent with Vendor's Tier 2 status under
POL-VRM-005.

## 5. Service Level Commitment
Vendor commits to 99.5% platform uptime measured monthly, excluding
scheduled maintenance windows communicated at least 5 business days in
advance. Failure to meet this commitment in any given month entitles the
Company to a service credit of 5% of the monthly-equivalent license fee
per 0.5% of uptime shortfall, up to a maximum of 25% credit in any month.

## 6. Termination
Either party may terminate for convenience with 60 days written notice.
Either party may terminate for cause with 15 days written notice and an
opportunity to cure. Upon termination, the Company shall receive a pro-rated
refund of any prepaid, unused license fees.

## 7. Liability and Indemnification
Vendor shall indemnify the Company against third-party claims arising from
intellectual property infringement related to the licensed platform.
Aggregate liability under this Agreement is capped at total fees paid in
the preceding 12 months, except for breaches of Section 4 (Data Privacy).

## 8. Governing Law
This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the state in which the
Company's headquarters is located.

## Approval
Approved by: H. Talbi, Director of Procurement
Date: 2026-03-10

# Procurement Policy
Document ID: POL-PROC-001
Version: 3.2
Effective Date: 2025-01-01
Owner: Procurement Department

## 1. Purpose
This policy governs the procurement of goods and services, including contract
approval, supplier selection, and payment terms for all vendor agreements.

## 2. Approval Thresholds
| Contract Value (USD) | Required Approver |
|---|---|
| Under $10,000 | Department Manager |
| $10,000 - $50,000 | Director |
| $50,000 - $250,000 | VP of Procurement |
| Over $250,000 | Chief Financial Officer + Legal Review |

Any contract exceeding $250,000 requires a mandatory legal review prior to
signature. Contracts cannot be executed without evidence of the required
approval level being obtained.

## 3. Advance Payment
Advance payment to suppliers is **not permitted** except under the following
conditions:
- The supplier is a new vendor with fewer than 2 prior transactions and the
  advance does not exceed 20% of total contract value, OR
- Advance payment is explicitly approved in writing by the VP of Procurement.

All other payment must follow standard net-30 terms from invoice receipt,
unless otherwise negotiated and documented in the contract's payment schedule.

## 4. Mandatory Contract Clauses
Every supplier contract must include, at minimum:
1. Scope of work / deliverables
2. Payment terms and schedule
3. Contract validity period (start and end dates)
4. Termination conditions
5. Data privacy and confidentiality clause (see Information Security Policy
   POL-SEC-002 for required language)
6. Liability and indemnification terms

Contracts missing any of the above are considered **non-compliant** and must
be flagged for revision before approval.

## 5. Invoice Tolerance
Invoices submitted against an active contract must not exceed the approved
contract value by more than **5%** without a formal contract amendment on
file. Invoices exceeding this tolerance must be flagged as a compliance
warning and routed back to the contract owner for review.

## 6. Supplier Verification
All invoices must be validated against the supplier name and tax ID recorded
in the original contract. Mismatches must be treated as a compliance failure,
not a warning, and escalated immediately.

## 7. Contract Termination
Contracts may be terminated for cause (breach, non-performance) with 15 days
written notice, or for convenience with 30 days written notice, unless a
different notice period is explicitly negotiated in the contract.

# Vendor Risk Management Policy
Document ID: POL-VRM-005
Version: 4.0
Effective Date: 2025-08-01
Owner: Enterprise Risk Management

## 1. Purpose and Scope
This policy establishes the framework for assessing, monitoring, and
mitigating risks associated with third-party vendors and suppliers across
their full engagement lifecycle, from onboarding through offboarding. It
applies to all vendors with access to Company systems, data, facilities, or
that provide services material to Company operations.

## 2. Vendor Risk Tiers
Vendors are classified into one of four risk tiers at onboarding and
reassessed annually or upon material change in scope:

### Tier 1 — Critical
Vendors with access to Restricted data, core production systems, or whose
failure would materially disrupt operations. Requires:
- Annual on-site or virtual security audit
- SOC 2 Type II report (or equivalent) on file, renewed annually
- Business continuity plan review
- Executive sponsor sign-off at onboarding and each renewal
- Quarterly business review meetings

### Tier 2 — High
Vendors with access to Confidential data or systems supporting important
but non-core functions. Requires:
- Security questionnaire completed annually
- SOC 2 Type I or equivalent attestation
- Semi-annual business review

### Tier 3 — Moderate
Vendors with access to Internal data only, no direct system access.
Requires:
- Security questionnaire at onboarding, refreshed every 2 years
- Standard contractual data protection clauses

### Tier 4 — Low
Vendors with no access to Company data or systems (e.g., facilities,
catering). Requires:
- Standard procurement onboarding only; no additional risk assessment

## 3. Onboarding Requirements
Before a contract can be executed with a new vendor, Procurement must:
1. Determine the appropriate risk tier based on data/system access scope
2. Confirm the vendor has completed all tier-appropriate assessments
3. Verify insurance coverage meets minimum thresholds (see Section 6)
4. Confirm the contract includes all mandatory clauses per Procurement
   Policy POL-PROC-001 and, where applicable, the data privacy clause
   required by Information Security Policy POL-SEC-002
5. Screen the vendor against sanctions and watch lists

Contracts executed without completing tier-appropriate onboarding steps are
considered non-compliant regardless of contract value.

## 4. Ongoing Monitoring
- Tier 1 and Tier 2 vendors must be reassessed at least annually.
- Any security incident involving a vendor (breach, outage, data loss) must
  trigger an immediate off-cycle risk reassessment.
- Vendor risk scores must be reviewed by Enterprise Risk Management before
  any contract renewal or amendment increasing scope of data access.

## 5. Fourth-Party (Subcontractor) Risk
Vendors that use subcontractors to fulfill contracted services must
disclose all subcontractors with access to Company data. The vendor remains
fully liable for subcontractor compliance with this policy and the
underlying contract's data protection terms. Undisclosed subcontracting
that involves data access is treated as a material breach.

## 6. Insurance Requirements
Minimum insurance coverage by tier:

| Tier | General Liability | Cyber Liability | Professional Liability |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tier 1 | $2,000,000 | $5,000,000 | $2,000,000 |
| Tier 2 | $1,000,000 | $2,000,000 | $1,000,000 |
| Tier 3 | $500,000 | $1,000,000 | Not required |
| Tier 4 | $500,000 | Not required | Not required |

Proof of insurance must be on file before contract execution and renewed
annually; lapses must be flagged and may trigger contract suspension.

## 7. Offboarding
At contract termination or expiration, the vendor must:
1. Return or securely destroy all Company data within 30 days, with
   written certification of destruction for Tier 1 and Tier 2 vendors
2. Have all system access revoked within 24 hours of termination
3. Complete a final risk closure review documenting any outstanding issues

## 8. Exceptions
Any exception to this policy requires written approval from the Chief Risk
Officer and must be time-bound with a defined remediation plan. Exceptions
cannot be granted for Tier 1 vendors without additional Board Risk Committee
notification.

## 9. Roles and Responsibilities
- **Procurement**: initial tier classification, onboarding checklist
  completion, contract clause verification
- **Enterprise Risk Management**: ongoing monitoring, annual reassessments,
  exception approvals below CRO threshold
- **Information Security**: security questionnaire review, breach response
  coordination, SOC 2 report evaluation
- **Legal**: contract clause sufficiency review for Tier 1 and Tier 2
  vendors
- **Business Owner**: day-to-day vendor relationship management and
  escalation of performance or risk concerns

## 10. Related Documents
- Procurement Policy (POL-PROC-001)
- Information Security Policy (POL-SEC-002)
- Payment Policy (POL-PAY-003)
- SOP: Contract Approval Process (SOP-CA-010)

# Data Retention and Records Management Policy
Document ID: POL-DRM-006
Version: 2.3
Effective Date: 2025-10-01
Owner: Legal & Records Management

## 1. Purpose and Scope
This policy establishes retention periods and disposal requirements for
contracts, invoices, compliance records, and related documentation
generated or received in connection with the Company's procurement and
contract compliance activities. It applies to all business units, and to
any third party acting as a records custodian on the Company's behalf.

## 2. Retention Schedule
| Record Type | Minimum Retention | Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| Executed contracts (all values) | 7 years | From contract expiration or termination |
| Contract amendments | 7 years | Same as parent contract |
| Invoices and payment records | 7 years | From date of payment |
| Legal review documentation | 7 years | From contract execution date |
| Vendor risk assessments (Tier 1/2) | 5 years | From assessment date |
| Vendor risk assessments (Tier 3/4) | 3 years | From assessment date |
| ServiceNow compliance incidents | 5 years | From incident closure |
| Data privacy impact assessments | 7 years | From assessment date |
| Insurance certificates | 3 years past expiry | From certificate expiration |
| Contract compliance audit reports | 10 years | From audit completion |

Retention periods represent minimums. Records subject to active litigation,
regulatory inquiry, or audit hold must be retained until the hold is
formally lifted by Legal, regardless of the schedule above.

## 3. Records Format and Accessibility
Records may be retained in their original format (paper or electronic) or
converted to a durable electronic format, provided the conversion preserves
legibility and the record's evidentiary integrity. Records ingested into
the Contract Compliance Assistant's knowledge base must retain their
original source document alongside any derived embeddings or extracted
text, so that a human reviewer can always trace a finding back to the
original file.

## 4. Legal Hold Process
When Legal issues a litigation hold notice, all custodians of potentially
relevant records must suspend any scheduled disposal for those records
immediately. The Contract Compliance Assistant's automated retention
enforcement (see Section 6) must support a hold flag that overrides
standard disposal scheduling on a per-document basis.

## 5. Disposal Requirements
Upon expiration of the applicable retention period, and absent an active
legal hold, records must be disposed of securely:
- Electronic records: permanent deletion including backups and archived
  copies, following the secure deletion standard referenced in the
  Information Security Policy (POL-SEC-002)
- Physical records: cross-cut shredding or certified secure destruction
  service

Disposal of Tier 1 or Tier 2 vendor-related records (per POL-VRM-005)
requires a documented disposal log entry, including record type, date
range covered, and the name of the individual authorizing disposal.

## 6. System Requirements
Any system storing contract, invoice, or compliance records — including
this application's vector database and document store — must:
1. Tag each ingested document with its record type and retention trigger
   date at ingestion time
2. Support flagging individual documents or record sets as under legal
   hold, which suspends any automated disposal for that record
3. Generate a disposal-eligibility report on a quarterly basis for Legal
   and Records Management review before any bulk deletion occurs
4. Log all disposal actions with timestamp, record identifier, and
   authorizing user

Automated bulk deletion without human review is not permitted under any
circumstance, even for records that have clearly exceeded their retention
period.

## 7. Roles and Responsibilities
- **Records Management**: maintains the retention schedule, coordinates
  quarterly disposal review cycles
- **Legal**: issues and lifts litigation holds, approves disposal of
  legally sensitive record categories
- **IT/Engineering**: implements and maintains system-level retention
  tagging, hold flags, and disposal logging described in Section 6
- **Business Owners**: identify records that may be subject to hold due to
  known disputes or investigations, even before Legal formally issues a
  hold notice

## 8. Exceptions
Deviations from the standard retention schedule (either shorter or longer
retention) require written approval from both Legal and Records Management,
documented with a business or regulatory justification, and reviewed
annually.

## 9. Related Documents
- Procurement Policy (POL-PROC-001)
- Information Security Policy (POL-SEC-002)
- Vendor Risk Management Policy (POL-VRM-005)
- SOP: Contract Renewal (SOP-CR-012)

# Information Security Policy
Document ID: POL-SEC-002
Version: 2.1
Effective Date: 2025-03-15
Owner: Information Security Office

## 1. Purpose
This policy defines minimum data protection and confidentiality requirements
that must be reflected in any contract where a third party may access,
process, store, or transmit company data.

## 2. Mandatory Data Privacy Clause
Any contract involving a supplier, vendor, or partner that will have access
to company data — including customer data, employee data, or confidential
business information — **must** include a data privacy clause covering:

1. Data ownership and permitted use restrictions
2. Data retention and secure deletion requirements at contract end
3. Breach notification timeline (must not exceed 72 hours from discovery)
4. Compliance with applicable data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA
   where applicable)
5. Right to audit the supplier's data handling practices

**Contracts that do not contain this clause are non-compliant and must be
rejected or returned for revision before approval, regardless of contract
value.**

## 3. Data Classification
All data shared with third parties under a contract must be classified
(Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted) and the classification must
determine the required security controls, which should be referenced in the
contract's data privacy clause.

## 4. Subcontractor Restrictions
Suppliers may not share company data with subcontractors or downstream
vendors unless explicitly permitted in the contract and the subcontractor
agrees to equivalent data protection terms.

## 5. Enforcement
Contract reviewers must verify the presence of a compliant data privacy
clause during the Contract Review workflow. This is a mandatory check and
cannot be waived by a Department Manager — waivers require sign-off from the
Information Security Office.

# Confidentiality Policy
Document ID: POL-CONF-004
Version: 1.0
Effective Date: 2025-05-01

All employees, contractors, and suppliers engaged under a Company agreement
must treat any non-public business information as confidential and may not
disclose it to third parties without prior written authorization from the
Company. This obligation survives termination of the underlying contract
for a period of 3 years.

# Payment Policy
Document ID: POL-PAY-003
Version: 1.4
Effective Date: 2025-06-01
Owner: Finance Department

## 1. Purpose
Defines payment terms, schedules, and controls for supplier invoices issued
against approved contracts.

## 2. Standard Payment Terms
- Default payment terms are **Net 30** from the date of invoice receipt,
  unless the contract specifies otherwise.
- Early payment discounts (e.g., 2/10 Net 30) may be applied only if
  explicitly stated in the contract's payment schedule.

## 3. Payment Schedule Compliance
Invoice payment schedules must match the schedule defined in the governing
contract. Any deviation (different due date, different milestone structure)
must be flagged as a warning during invoice validation.

## 4. Milestone-Based Payments
For contracts with milestone-based deliverables, payment may only be
released after the corresponding milestone has been marked complete and
accepted. Invoices submitted before milestone completion must be rejected.

## 5. Overpayment Prevention
Finance and the Contract Compliance system must jointly verify:
- Invoice amount does not exceed the remaining approved contract balance
- Cumulative payments to date do not exceed total contract value unless an
  approved amendment increasing contract value is on file

Any invoice that would cause cumulative payments to exceed contract value
must be blocked pending amendment approval.

## 6. Currency and Rounding
All contracts and invoices must be evaluated in the currency specified in
the contract. Cross-currency invoices require conversion using the exchange
rate documented at contract signing, not the rate at invoice date, unless
the contract specifies a floating-rate clause.

# SOP: Invoice Validation Against Contract
Document ID: SOP-IV-011
Version: 1.0
Effective Date: 2025-04-10
Owner: Finance & Procurement

## Purpose
Defines how an invoice submitted against an existing contract should be
validated before payment approval.

## Procedure

### Step 1 — Retrieve Governing Contract
Locate the original approved contract associated with the supplier and
purchase/contract ID referenced on the invoice.

### Step 2 — Field-Level Validation
Compare the invoice against the contract on:
1. **Supplier name and tax ID** — must match exactly. Mismatch = Fail.
2. **Invoice amount** — must not exceed contract value, and must not exceed
   remaining balance if partial payments have already occurred. Amount
   exceeding the 5% tolerance defined in Procurement Policy (POL-PROC-001)
   = Warning; amount exceeding total contract value = Fail.
3. **Payment schedule** — due date and milestone alignment with contract
   terms. Deviation = Warning.
4. **Deliverables referenced** — must correspond to deliverables defined in
   the contract scope of work. Unlisted deliverables = Warning, pending
   contract owner clarification.
5. **Contract validity period** — invoice date must fall within the
   contract's active start and end dates. Invoice outside this window = Fail.

### Step 3 — Policy Cross-Check
Validate advance payment requests against Procurement Policy Section 3, and
payment terms against Payment Policy (POL-PAY-003).

### Step 4 — Historical Context
Check ServiceNow for prior incidents involving this supplier or contract
(e.g., past overpayments, disputed invoices) to inform the reviewer's
decision.

### Step 5 — Report Generation
Produce a structured finding set (Pass / Warning / Fail per field) with
citations to the specific contract clause and policy section used for each
determination.

# SOP: Contract Renewal
Document ID: SOP-CR-012
Version: 1.0
Effective Date: 2025-09-01

Contract owners must initiate renewal review at least 45 days before
contract expiration. Renewal requires reconfirming supplier standing (no
open Tier 1 risk findings), reapplying the current Procurement Policy
approval threshold based on updated contract value, and reissuing the data
privacy clause if the Information Security Policy has been revised since
original signature. Contracts not renewed or terminated by their expiration
date automatically lapse and require a new full approval cycle to reinstate.

# SOP: Contract Approval Process
Document ID: SOP-CA-010
Version: 1.2
Effective Date: 2025-02-01
Owner: Legal & Procurement

## Purpose
Standardizes the steps required to review and approve a new supplier
contract before execution.

## Procedure

### Step 1 — Intake
Contract owner submits the drafted contract along with supplier details and
estimated total contract value.

### Step 2 — Policy Compliance Check
Contract is checked against:
- Procurement Policy (POL-PROC-001) for approval thresholds and mandatory
  clauses
- Information Security Policy (POL-SEC-002) for data privacy clause
  requirements

Any missing mandatory clause must be logged as a **Fail** finding, not a
warning, since it blocks approval.

### Step 3 — Legal Review (if applicable)
Required whenever:
- Contract value exceeds $250,000, OR
- Contract involves data sharing with a third party, OR
- Contract includes non-standard termination or liability terms

Legal review omission for contracts requiring it is itself a critical
compliance failure and must be logged, even if all other clauses are
present.

### Step 4 — Approval Routing
Contract routed to the approver defined by the Procurement Policy threshold
table based on total contract value.

### Step 5 — Execution
Once approved, contract is signed and stored, and becomes the governing
document for all downstream validations (invoices, amendments).

## Common Failure Points (for reviewer reference)
- Missing data privacy clause (most frequent finding)
- Contract routed to wrong approval level for its value
- Legal review skipped for high-value contracts
- Payment schedule not clearly defined

# SOP: Vendor Onboarding and Offboarding
Document ID: SOP-VOB-013
Version: 2.0
Effective Date: 2025-11-15
Owner: Procurement & Enterprise Risk Management

## Purpose
Defines the end-to-end process for bringing a new vendor into an active
contractual relationship and formally closing out a vendor relationship at
contract end, ensuring both procurement and risk requirements are met at
each stage.

## Part A — Onboarding

### Step 1 — Intake and Risk Tier Determination
Business owner submits a vendor intake request specifying the scope of
services and the type of data or system access required. Procurement, in
coordination with Enterprise Risk Management, determines the vendor's risk
tier per Vendor Risk Management Policy (POL-VRM-005) Section 2.

### Step 2 — Tier-Appropriate Assessment
Based on the assigned tier:
- **Tier 1**: Vendor must submit SOC 2 Type II report, complete a full
  security questionnaire, and undergo an initial security audit before
  contract execution.
- **Tier 2**: Vendor must submit SOC 2 Type I (or equivalent) and complete
  the standard security questionnaire.
- **Tier 3**: Vendor completes the standard security questionnaire only.
- **Tier 4**: No additional assessment required beyond standard
  procurement intake.

Contracts cannot be routed for approval until the tier-appropriate
assessment is complete and on file.

### Step 3 — Sanctions and Watch List Screening
Procurement screens the vendor's legal entity name against applicable
sanctions and watch lists before proceeding. A positive match requires
escalation to Legal and halts onboarding pending resolution.

### Step 4 — Insurance Verification
Vendor must provide certificates of insurance meeting the minimum coverage
thresholds defined in POL-VRM-005 Section 6 for their assigned tier.
Coverage below the required threshold must be remediated (increased
coverage or a documented risk acceptance from the Chief Risk Officer)
before contract execution.

### Step 5 — Contract Drafting and Clause Verification
Contract must include all mandatory clauses per Procurement Policy
(POL-PROC-001) Section 4, and the data privacy clause required by
Information Security Policy (POL-SEC-002) if the vendor will access
Company data. Reference SOP: Contract Approval Process (SOP-CA-010) for the
full approval routing procedure.

### Step 6 — System Provisioning (if applicable)
For vendors requiring system access, IT provisions access strictly scoped
to the minimum required for the contracted services, following the
principle of least privilege. Access provisioning must not occur before
contract execution.

### Step 7 — Onboarding Confirmation
Procurement records confirmation that all prior steps are complete before
the vendor is marked active in the vendor management system and the
contract becomes the governing document for future invoice validation.

## Part B — Offboarding

### Step 1 — Offboarding Trigger
Offboarding is initiated upon contract expiration without renewal,
termination for convenience, or termination for cause.

### Step 2 — Access Revocation
IT revokes all system access within 24 hours of the offboarding trigger, as
required by POL-VRM-005 Section 7. This applies regardless of the reason
for offboarding.

### Step 3 — Data Return or Destruction
Vendor returns or destroys all Company data within 30 days per POL-VRM-005
Section 7 and Data Retention and Records Management Policy (POL-DRM-006).
For Tier 1 and Tier 2 vendors, written certification of destruction is
required and must be retained per the retention schedule in POL-DRM-006.

### Step 4 — Final Invoice Reconciliation
Finance confirms all outstanding invoices have been validated and paid, or
formally disputed, before the vendor relationship is closed in the system.
Any open disputes must be documented with a resolution owner and target
date.

### Step 5 — Risk Closure Review
Enterprise Risk Management conducts a closure review documenting any
outstanding risk findings, open security incidents, or unresolved audit
items associated with the vendor, per POL-VRM-005 Section 7.

### Step 6 — Records Retention
All contract, invoice, and risk assessment records associated with the
vendor relationship are retained per the schedule in POL-DRM-006 — records
are not deleted at offboarding, only the active vendor relationship is
closed.

## Common Failure Points
- Contract executed before required security assessment is complete
- System access provisioned before contract execution (Step 6, Part A)
- Access not revoked within the 24-hour window at offboarding
- Missing destruction certification for Tier 1/2 vendor offboarding
- Records deleted at offboarding instead of following the retention
  schedule

# Knowledge Article: How Long Does Confidentiality Last After a Contract Ends?
Article ID: KA-0163
Category: Legal

Per the Confidentiality Policy (POL-CONF-004), confidentiality obligations
survive contract termination for 3 years. This applies regardless of why
the contract ended (expiration, termination for convenience, or termination
for cause) and cannot be shortened without Legal approval.

# Knowledge Article: Procurement & Contract FAQ
Article ID: KA-0142
Category: Procurement
Last Updated: 2025-11-02

## Q: What is the approval threshold for a new contract?
A: It depends on total contract value. Under $10,000 requires only a
Department Manager. Between $10,000 and $50,000 requires Director approval.
Between $50,000 and $250,000 requires VP of Procurement approval. Anything
over $250,000 requires both CFO approval and a mandatory Legal Review. See
Procurement Policy POL-PROC-001, Section 2.

## Q: Is advance payment allowed?
A: Generally no. Advance payment is only allowed for new suppliers (fewer
than 2 prior transactions) up to 20% of contract value, or with explicit
written approval from the VP of Procurement. See POL-PROC-001, Section 3.

## Q: Which policy governs contract termination?
A: Procurement Policy POL-PROC-001, Section 7. Standard terms are 15 days
notice for termination for cause, or 30 days for termination for
convenience, unless the contract negotiates a different period.

## Q: What clauses are mandatory in every contract?
A: Scope of work, payment terms, contract validity period, termination
conditions, a data privacy/confidentiality clause, and liability/
indemnification terms. See POL-PROC-001 Section 4 and POL-SEC-002 for the
specific data privacy clause requirements.

## Q: What happens if an invoice exceeds the contract value?
A: If it exceeds by more than 5% without an approved amendment on file, it
must be flagged and routed back to the contract owner. If it exceeds the
total contract value outright, this is a Fail, not a Warning, and payment
must be blocked pending an amendment. See POL-PROC-001 Section 5 and
Payment Policy POL-PAY-003 Section 5.

## Q: Does every contract need a legal review?
A: Only if it exceeds $250,000, involves third-party data sharing, or has
non-standard termination/liability terms. See SOP-CA-010 Step 3.

# Knowledge Article: Vendor Risk Tiers Quick Reference
Article ID: KA-0156
Category: Vendor Risk

Tier 1 = Critical (core systems/Restricted data) — annual audit + SOC 2
Type II required. Tier 2 = High — annual questionnaire + SOC 2 Type I.
Tier 3 = Moderate — questionnaire every 2 years. Tier 4 = Low — standard
onboarding only. Full detail: Vendor Risk Management Policy POL-VRM-005.

# Knowledge Article: Contract Compliance Program Overview
Article ID: KA-0201
Category: Program Overview
Last Updated: 2026-01-10

## What This Program Covers
The Contract Compliance program governs how contracts, invoices, and
related documents are reviewed, validated, and monitored across their
lifecycle, from initial drafting through renewal or termination. It brings
together requirements from several policies and SOPs that, read
individually, can be hard to apply consistently. This article summarizes
how they fit together.

## The Core Documents and How They Relate
- **Procurement Policy (POL-PROC-001)** sets the baseline: approval
  thresholds by contract value, mandatory clauses every contract must
  contain, advance payment restrictions, and invoice tolerance rules.
- **Information Security Policy (POL-SEC-002)** adds a specific
  requirement on top of the Procurement Policy's general mandatory-clause
  list: any contract involving data access must include a compliant data
  privacy clause, and this cannot be waived below the Information Security
  Office.
- **Payment Policy (POL-PAY-003)** governs how invoices are paid once a
  contract is active — standard terms, milestone-based release, and
  overpayment prevention.
- **Vendor Risk Management Policy (POL-VRM-005)** layers additional
  requirements on top of the above based on a vendor's risk tier —
  higher-risk vendors need deeper security assessments, insurance
  coverage, and more frequent reassessment.
- **Data Retention and Records Management Policy (POL-DRM-006)** governs
  what happens to all the records this program generates — contracts,
  invoices, risk assessments — after the relationship ends.
- **Confidentiality Policy (POL-CONF-004)** sets the default confidentiality
  survival period referenced in most contract templates.

## How a Contract Moves Through the Program
1. **Intake and risk tiering** (SOP-VOB-013, Part A) — before drafting even
   finishes, the vendor's risk tier is determined, which decides what
   assessments are required.
2. **Drafting and clause verification** — the contract must satisfy both
   the general mandatory clauses (POL-PROC-001) and, where applicable, the
   data privacy clause (POL-SEC-002).
3. **Approval routing** (SOP-CA-010) — routed based on contract value per
   the Procurement Policy threshold table, with mandatory legal review
   triggered above $250,000 or for data-sharing/non-standard terms.
4. **Execution** — once approved, the contract becomes the governing
   document for all future invoice validation.
5. **Invoice validation** (SOP-IV-011) — every invoice submitted against
   the contract is checked field-by-field: supplier identity, amount,
   schedule, deliverables, and validity window.
6. **Renewal or offboarding** (SOP-CR-012, SOP-VOB-013 Part B) — as the
   contract approaches expiration, either a renewal review or a formal
   offboarding process is triggered, both of which reference back to the
   original policies to reconfirm nothing has drifted out of compliance.
7. **Retention** (POL-DRM-006) — throughout and after this lifecycle, every
   record generated is retained according to its type, with legal holds
   able to override standard disposal at any point.

## Why Findings Are Categorized Pass / Warning / Fail
Not every deviation carries the same weight. A missing mandatory clause or
a supplier name mismatch is treated as a **Fail** because it represents a
compliance gap that blocks approval or payment outright. An invoice that
exceeds tolerance but has a plausible explanation, or a payment schedule
that deviates slightly from the contract, is typically a **Warning** —
something a human reviewer should look at, but not necessarily a blocker.
Understanding this distinction matters when interpreting the Assistant's
compliance reports: a report full of Warnings is not the same risk level
as one containing even a single Fail.

## Where ServiceNow Fits In
Historical ServiceNow incidents are not policy — they don't define a rule
the Assistant enforces. They exist to give a human reviewer context: "this
exact pattern has caused a problem before." A supplier name mismatch
finding becomes more actionable when the reviewer can also see that the
same supplier had a similar incident logged eighteen months ago.
